title: This Tick Can Give You a Meat Allergy
hook: The lone star tick is spreading across much of the U.S. — and its bite can trigger alpha-gal syndrome, a delayed allergic reaction to red meat.
key_points: The lone star tick's range now covers much of the eastern and central U.S.
Its bite can trigger alpha-gal syndrome, an allergy to a sugar molecule found in red meat.
Unlike most food allergies, reactions are delayed — often hours after eating meat, not minutes.
The same tick-avoidance basics that prevent Lyme disease also cut the risk of alpha-gal.
content_html: Most people worry about ticks because of Lyme disease. But the lone star tick, whose range now covers much of the eastern and central U.S., carries a stranger risk: a bite can trigger alpha-gal syndrome, an allergy to a sugar molecule called alpha-gal that's found in red meat. NPR's Terry Gross discussed the tick and the syndrome with New Yorker writer Burkhard Bilger.
extra_html: What makes alpha-gal syndrome unusual is the delay. Instead of the near-instant reaction typical of a peanut or shellfish allergy, symptoms after eating beef, pork, or lamb can take hours to appear — hives, stomach pain, or in severe cases anaphylaxis — which makes the tick-bite connection easy to miss. There's no cure beyond avoiding red meat (and sometimes other mammal products) after developing the allergy, so prevention comes down to the same habits that guard against Lyme disease: repellent, permethrin-treated clothing, and a full-body tick check after time outdoors.

related.title: How to Protect Yourself From Ticks
related.hook: Tick season is here, and a single bite can pass on Lyme and other diseases. A few simple habits sharply cut the risk.

flashcards.prompt: What makes an alpha-gal allergic reaction different from a typical food allergy?
flashcards.back_html: It's delayed — symptoms from eating red meat often show up hours later, instead of the near-immediate reaction typical of most food allergies. That delay can make the cause hard to trace back to a tick bite.

flashcards.explanation_html: The lone star tick's bite can sensitize the immune system to alpha-gal, a sugar molecule found in red meat — turning a tick encounter into a lasting meat allergy.
